learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Readiness checks are low stakes; an unresolved fresh re-entry returns control without target exit credit.

items.title: Readiness check: energy accounting
items.prompt: A closed system absorbs 35 kJ of heat while 12 kJ of work is done on it. Using ΔU = q + w with both transfers positive into the system, what is ΔU?
items.directions: Choose one response or leave the item unanswered. This check is low stakes and may return you to prerequisite study.

items.title: Guided practice: reaction direction
items.prompt: The combustion equation for one mole of a fuel releases 640 kJ at constant pressure. What enthalpy belongs to the reaction as written?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Less support: reverse a thermochemical equation
items.prompt: For P → Q, ΔH = −72 kJ/mol. What value belongs to the reversed equation Q → P?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: On your own: scale the equation
items.prompt: For 2 R → S, ΔH = +90 kJ. What is ΔH for 6 R → 3 S under the same conditions?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Near exit: combine consecutive steps
items.prompt: A → B has ΔH = +40 kJ/mol, and B → C has ΔH = −15 kJ/mol. What is ΔH for A → C?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Changed exit: use a bond inventory
items.prompt: Estimate ΔH for H₂ + Cl₂ → 2 HCl using H–H = 436 kJ/mol, Cl–Cl = 243 kJ/mol, and H–Cl = 431 kJ/mol.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: make an intermediate cancel
items.prompt: An intermediate X appears on the product side of two equations, but the target contains no X. What transformation is required before adding the equations?
options: Add the equations unchanged and delete X afterward
Reverse one equation and reverse its ΔH sign
Reverse one equation but retain its original ΔH sign
Multiply both equations by −1 without changing direction
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: combine a reversed step
items.prompt: M → N has ΔH = −55 kJ/mol, and P → N has ΔH = +20 kJ/mol. What is ΔH for M → P?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: choose the bond-energy subtraction
items.prompt: Which expression correctly estimates reaction enthalpy from average bond energies?
options: Sum formed bond energies minus sum broken bond energies
Sum all listed bond energies without tracking side
Sum broken bond energies minus sum formed bond energies
Use only the single strongest bond in the reaction
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: hydrogenate a double bond
items.prompt: Estimate ΔH for C₂H₄ + H₂ → C₂H₆ using C=C = 614, H–H = 436, C–C = 347, and C–H = 413 kJ/mol. Count the net changes only.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Readiness check: entropy direction
items.prompt: A pure gas condenses to a liquid at constant temperature. Considering only the substance, what is the sign of ΔS for this change?
items.directions: Choose one response or leave the item unanswered. This check is low stakes and may return you to prerequisite study.

items.title: Guided practice: calculate ΔG
items.prompt: At 298 K, a process has ΔH = −40.0 kJ/mol and ΔS = −100 J/(mol·K). What is ΔG?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Less support: classify the sign pair
items.prompt: A reaction has ΔH < 0 and ΔS > 0. Which temperature statement is supported for ΔG?
options: ΔG is negative at every positive temperature
ΔG is positive at every positive temperature
ΔG is negative only below a crossover temperature
ΔG is negative only above a crossover temperature
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: On your own: identify the favorable regime
items.prompt: For a process with ΔH > 0 and ΔS > 0, when can the forward process have ΔG < 0?
options: Only when temperature is low enough
At high enough T for TΔS to exceed ΔH
At every temperature because entropy is positive
At no temperature because enthalpy is positive
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Near exit: evaluate a new condition
items.prompt: At 400 K, a reaction has ΔH = +24 kJ/mol and ΔS = +80 J/(mol·K). What is ΔG?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Changed exit: determine a temperature interval
items.prompt: A reaction has ΔH = −60 kJ/mol and ΔS = −150 J/(mol·K). For which temperatures is ΔG < 0?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: make energy units compatible
items.prompt: ΔH is reported in kJ/mol and ΔS in J/(mol·K). What must happen before evaluating ΔH − TΔS?
options: Convert both energy terms to the same unit
Convert kelvin to degrees Celsius before multiplying
Discard the sign on ΔS and compare magnitudes only
Divide ΔH by temperature and add the entropy value
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: calculate with converted entropy
items.prompt: At 350 K, a process has ΔH = +18 kJ/mol and ΔS = +60 J/(mol·K). What is ΔG?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: locate the crossover
items.prompt: When ΔH and ΔS have the same sign and a crossover exists, which condition locates it?
options: Set ΔG = ΔH + TΔS and solve for pressure
Set ΔG = 0 and solve T = ΔH/ΔS
Set ΔS = 0 and solve T = ΔG/ΔH
Set ΔH = 0 and choose the highest temperature
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: infer a high-temperature regime
items.prompt: A process has ΔH = +45 kJ/mol and ΔS = +150 J/(mol·K). Which temperature condition gives ΔG < 0?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Readiness check: equilibrium shift
items.prompt: For A ⇌ B, extra A is added at constant temperature while all other conditions are unchanged. Which immediate equilibrium response is predicted before a new equilibrium is established?
options: The system shifts toward A and produces still more A
The forward and reverse reactions both stop
The system shifts toward B, consuming some added A
items.directions: Choose one response or leave the item unanswered. This check is low stakes and may return you to prerequisite study.

items.title: Guided practice: read the sign relation
items.prompt: At a fixed positive temperature, K = 50 for a reaction. What sign must ΔG° have?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Less support: identify the boundary case
items.prompt: At a stated temperature, a reaction has K = 1. Which standard free-energy value is consistent with this?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: On your own: infer equilibrium position
items.prompt: A reaction has ΔG° > 0 at a stated temperature. Which equilibrium statement follows for the reaction as written?
options: K = 1 with equal standard free energies
K is determined only by the catalyst
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Near exit: interpret a large K
items.prompt: At 310 K, a reaction has K = 100. Which paired conclusion is supported?
options: ΔG° > 0 and products are favored at equilibrium
ΔG° = 0 and neither side is favored
ΔG° < 0 and the reaction must be rapid
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Changed exit: add a catalyst
items.prompt: A catalyst lowers the activation energies of both directions for A ⇌ B at fixed temperature. What changes after the catalyst is added?
options: K increases because products form faster
ΔG° becomes more negative while K stays fixed
Faster equilibration; unchanged K and ΔG°
The reverse reaction stops once products appear
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: track the logarithm sign
items.prompt: Which sign chain is correct when 0 < K < 1 at positive temperature?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: interpret a small K
items.prompt: At a fixed temperature, a fresh reaction has K = 0.010. Which conclusion follows?
options: ΔG° is positive and reactants are favored
ΔG° is negative and reactants are favored
ΔG° is zero and products are favored
ΔG° is positive and the reaction cannot occur
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Repair: separate endpoints from barriers
items.prompt: On a reaction-energy profile, which feature can a catalyst change without changing the equilibrium constant at fixed temperature?
options: The free-energy difference between products and reactants
The identities and standard states of the products
The activation barrier along the reaction pathway
The value of RT in the equilibrium relation
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: scale both rate constants
items.prompt: For an elementary reversible step, a catalyst makes both forward and reverse rate constants five times larger at the same temperature. What is the most direct consequence?
options: The equilibrium constant becomes five times larger
The equilibrium constant becomes five times smaller
The standard free-energy change becomes zero
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it before feedback is released.
